neighbours.label: a noun or brand naming a business as an entity (' company', ' firm', ' manufacturer', Samsung), as opposed to a person or thing
fire: Investors read a company statement about the merger on Friday.
I called the company about a refund for the broken heater.
Workers at the company were told about the layoffs by email.
She researched the firm before applying for the sales job.
You can find the manual on the manufacturer's site under support.
Last year the whole company moved its offices to Denver.
He was looking through Samsung's support pages for a firmware update.
Any company can register a trademark for a small fee.
quiet: Investors read a personal statement about the merger on Friday.
I called the plumber about a refund for the broken heater.
Workers on the night shift were told about the layoffs by email.
She researched the salary before applying for the sales job.
You can find the manual in the glove box under the papers.
Last year the whole family moved its things to Denver.
He was looking through the support pages for a firmware update.
Any citizen can register a trademark for a small fee.

notes: ' company' dominates the card; the output promotes possessives, ' website', ' products'. Probe: other institutions (school, hospital, museum) also fire at 0.3-0.45, so the real distinction may be organisation rather than business. Near misses use people and things, not institutions.
